question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
answer:
North American Aviation built it.

Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

Columbia was Apollo 11's command module: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The command and service module was built by North American Aviation: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

North American Aviation was also the prime contractor for it: [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
answer:
Before launch, the heaters of oxygen tank No. 2 ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The investigating board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The notes also give this background:
- The tank's thermostatic switches were built for 28 volts DC. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- The heater specification was later revised to 65 volts, but the switches were not changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- The board's report called the switch failure an oversight shared by all parties. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

question: How long before Kennedy's speech at Rice University did NASA announce its Apollo mission mode?

returned: apollo-1 | 2.33 | - [stated] Happened at Launch Complex 34 at Cape Kennedy (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)
apollo-11 | 2.13 | - [stated] Launched 1969-07-16 from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)

answer:
NASA announced the Apollo mission mode 63 days (9 weeks) before Kennedy's Rice University speech.

- NASA announced lunar orbit rendezvous as the mission mode on 11 July 1962. [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] NASA announced it as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- Kennedy gave the Rice speech on 12 September 1962. [[john-f-kennedy]] "[stated] Gave the 'We choose to go to the Moon' speech at Rice University on 1962-09-12 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The 63-day figure is my own calculation from those two dates: 20 days left in July, 31 in August and 12 in September. No note states it.

question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
answer:
Here are the 1970 dates the brain records for Apollo 13, in order. I copied each quoted fact line in full, including its leading tag.

- **1970-04-06:** Physicals took place, and the blood tests showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided and announced. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". Jack Swigert became command module pilot in place of Mattingly. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
